html:
The railway that runs the length of Vietnam, about 1,726 km from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City, built by the French between 1899 and 1936. It is still the backbone of the country's railways.

The plan was pushed by Paul Doumer, governor general of French Indochina, who wanted railways to tie the colony together and open it to French trade. It was built in sections, by Vietnamese labourers, many of whom died in hard conditions. When the last gap opened in 1936, a train could run from Hanoi to Saigon on the metre gauge line, through Huế and along the coast. The French also built the line from Haiphong to Kunming in China.

The railway was cut and bombed many times in the wars that followed, the First Indochina War and the Vietnam War, and the country's division in 1954 split it in two. After reunification it was repaired and reopened on 31 December 1976, and the through trains became known as the Reunification Express. See Vietnam.
sum: The railway that runs the length of Vietnam, about 1,726 km from Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh City, built by the French between 1899 and 1936. It is still the backbone of the country's railways.
